compliance: Protected by plant breeders' rights (EU 60237); propagation for sale needs a licence.
cvs: 'Fire Power' – dwarf, red winter foliage · OBSESSED ('Seika') – upright, red new growth · 'Gulf Stream' – compact, bronze-red tints · 'Richmond' – taller, heavy berrying
foliage: evergreen; finely divided pinnate leaves, red when young and in cold weather
hardinessNote: Hardy through a cold UK winter, approximately -15 to -10°C.
pollination: not applicable; sold for its foliage
prune: Little needed. Remove dead or damaged stems in spring, and cut a few of the oldest stems to the base to keep it bushy.
resilience: Generally tough and trouble-free once established. Foliage can scorch in cold, drying winds. Pests: few significant pests in the UK.
toxicity: Toxic if eaten: all parts, especially the berries, contain cyanogenic compounds. Keep children, dogs and cats from chewing it.
uncertain: hardiness: Plantipp says -18°C, an Italian nursery -10 to -15°C; H5 taken between them, matching the deck's Nandina 'Twilight'
peak: year-round foliage, red strongest on new growth and in cold weather; Jan-Dec as on 'Twilight'
size: RHS 0.5–1 m in 2–5 years; Plantipp 60 × 50 cm
clay: RHS lists clay tolerance for the plant, kept blank pending a cultivar source
uses: Borders · containers · low hedging · patio planting · winter colour
visual: Marbled green, cream and pink leaves with red edges · fiery red new shoots and winter colour
water: Water regularly in the first season, then only in prolonged dry spells; pots need regular watering in summer.
